key_insights: Early Action is non-binding: student applies by ~November 1, hears back by mid-December, and keeps all options open until May 1 decision day
Early Decision is binding: if admitted, the student must enroll and withdraw all other applications, and can only apply ED to one school
Restrictive Early Action is non-binding but limits a student from applying early to most other schools simultaneously
Early Decision II is a second binding round with a January deadline, useful if a favorite school emerges later in the fall
The key financial risk of ED is committing before seeing any financial aid offers, losing the ability to compare packages across schools
Schools generally only release a student from an ED commitment if the aid package makes attendance truly unaffordable - a better offer elsewhere doesn't qualify
Recommends using each college's required net price calculator to estimate real cost before committing to ED
Suggests deciding between EA and ED using two yes/no questions: certainty about the top-choice school, and affordability confirmed by the net price calculator
